definition_zh: 占卜官；预言者；预示；预兆
definition_en: in ancient Rome, an official who interpreted omens; as a verb, to be a sign that something is likely to happen
core_image: 看鸟的飞行方向读出未来的祭司之眼
scene: 罗马城头，占卜官凝视群鸟划过天际的轨迹。The priests augured that the new colony would prosper.
sceneCN: 这里 augur 指「预言、预示」（第 2 个义项：作为动词预断吉凶）；句意：祭司们预卜新殖民地将会兴旺。

derivatives.zh: 占卜；预兆（augur + -y 名词后缀）
开创；举行就职典礼（同族词，出自占卜官主持开国之礼）
就职典礼；开创（inaugurate 的名词）

senses.title: A Roman diviner
senses.definition: in ancient Rome, a religious official who read omens, especially the flight of birds
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马解读征兆（尤其鸟飞之象）的宗教官员
senses.example: No Roman army marched before the augurs approved.
senses.exampleCN: 未经占卜官首肯，罗马军队一兵不发。
senses.why: The noun is the word's original office: a man whose job was to read the sky.
senses.whyCN: 名词是这个词的原初职位：以观天读象为业的人。

senses.title: To predict by omens
senses.definition: to predict or divine something by reading signs
senses.example: They augured the harvest from the autumn winds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凭秋风预断了收成。
senses.why: The official's act became a verb: what the augur did, anyone can augur.
senses.whyCN: 官职的行为化为动词：占卜官所做的事，人人皆可 augur。

senses.title: To be a sign of something coming
senses.definition: to be a sign that something is likely to happen in the future
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将来可能发生的迹象
senses.example: Rising orders augur a strong year for the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 订单攀升预示着工厂一年的好光景。
senses.why: Modern English keeps only the sign, not the ritual: events now play the birds.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语只保留了「征兆」而舍弃了仪式：如今扮演飞鸟的是事件本身。

senses.title: To augur well or ill
senses.definition: to promise good or bad outcomes, in the fixed phrases augur well and augur ill
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配 augur well / augur ill 中预示吉凶
senses.example: The calm sea augured well for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 平静的海面是渡航的好兆头。
senses.why: The auspicious side of divination survived in two idioms of good and bad signs.
senses.whyCN: 占卜的吉凶两面留存在「吉兆」「凶兆」两个习语之中。

senses.title: A prophet or soothsayer generally
senses.definition: any person who claims to foretell events, not only the Roman official
senses.definitionCN: 任何自称能预知未来的人，不限于罗马官员
senses.example: Street-corner augurs promised the crowds a golden age.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的预言者们向人群许诺黄金时代。
senses.why: Once the office was named, impostors borrowed its title.
senses.whyCN: 官职一旦得名，招摇撞骗者便借用其头衔。

senses.title: Omens and augury as practice
senses.definition: the practice or reading of omens, when the word appears in its noun-family forms
senses.definitionCN: 解读征兆的行为体系，见于其名词家族词形
senses.example: Bird flight was central to Roman augury.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟飞之象是罗马占卜术的核心。
senses.why: The practice needed a name, so augury grew beside augur.
senses.whyCN: 这门术数需要名字，augury 便在 augur 旁边生长出来。

senses.title: Authority founded on signs
senses.definition: power exercised by declaring what the signs permit, as the Roman augurs did over state acts
senses.definitionCN: 如罗马占卜官那样，借宣告征兆准许与否而行使的权力
senses.example: The augurs could block an election with a single negative sign.
senses.exampleCN: 占卜官一纸凶兆便可叫停一场选举。
senses.why: Reading signs was also ruling: the sky's verdicts stopped assemblies and wars.
senses.whyCN: 读象亦是执政：上天的裁决能叫停集会与战争。

senses.title: Inauguration, the bright descendant
senses.titleCN: 开国之礼；就职典礼（同族引申）
senses.definition: the founding rite that Roman augurs blessed, preserved in inaugurate and inauguration
senses.definitionCN: 罗马占卜官主持祝福的开创仪式，今存于 inaugurate、inauguration
senses.example: The president's inauguration echoes an ancient augural rite.
senses.exampleCN: 总统就职典礼可回溯到古老的占卜官仪式。
senses.why: Founding a city needed the birds' approval, so the rite took the augur's name.
senses.whyCN: 建城须得飞鸟认可，这项仪式便取了占卜官之名。

intro.en: Augur is a direct borrowing from Latin augur, the official diviner of Rome; the further root is debated, perhaps from avis, bird, plus gar- or agere, or from an old root meaning increase, the same family as augment.
intro.cn: augur 直接借自拉丁语 augur（罗马占卜官）；更早的词源有争议，或出自 avis「鸟」加 gar-/agere，或出自意为「增长」的老词根，与 augment 同族。

items.en: One proposed root *h₂eg- meant to drive or increase; another line links *awi-, bird. Both hypotheses remain open.
items.cn: 一说词根 *h₂eg- 意为「驱动、增长」；另一说联系 *awi-「鸟」。两种假说并存。

items.en: augur named the member of the priestly college who read omens from birds, sky, and sacred meals.
items.cn: 拉丁语 augur 指祭司团中凭飞鸟、天象与圣餐解读征兆的成员。

items.en: augurium meant divination or an omen, and augurare, to augur, the act of predicting.
items.cn: augurium 意为占卜或征兆，动词 augurare 意为预断。

items.en: inaugurare meant to consecrate with omens, the rite of founding cities and installing officials.
items.cn: inaugurare 意为「以征兆祝圣」，即建城与就任的仪式。

items.en: English took augur as noun and verb in the mid-sixteenth century, when classical learning was fashionable.
items.cn: 16 世纪中叶，正值古典学风盛行，英语同时借入 augur 的名、动两种用法。

items.en: Today the ritual is gone; augur survives mainly in augur well or ill, and inauguration keeps the festive descendant.
items.cn: 如今仪式已逝；augur 主要存于 augur well / ill，而就职典礼保留了其节庆后代。

note.en: Group one collects the aug- family and common look-alikes; group two collects neighboring omen and prediction words.
note.cn: 第一组收 aug- 词族及常见形近词；第二组收相邻的征兆与预言词。

entries.definition: divination or an omen; the noun family of augur.
entries.definitionCN: 占卜；预兆；augur 的名词家族。

entries.definition: majestic, from Latin augustus, on the same debated increase root; the link is plausible but not proven.
entries.definitionCN: 威严的，出自拉丁语 augustus，与 augur 或同属「增长」词根——关联可信但未成定论。

entries.definition: to increase, from augere; shares the proposed increase root.
entries.definitionCN: 增加，出自 augere「增长」；同属拟议中的「增长」词根。

entries.definition: a writer, from Latin auctor; similar sound, different family.
entries.definitionCN: 作者，出自拉丁语 auctor；读音相近，词族不同。

entries.definition: a drilling tool; pronounced the same, spelled one letter apart, unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 钻头；发音完全相同，仅一字母之差，词源无关。

entries.definition: an event believed to signal the future.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为预示未来的征兆。

entries.definition: to signal, often ominously, what is to come.
to foreshadow; a sign of what follows.
a person who claims to foretell the future.
one that announces the approach of something.

normalIntro.en: augur keeps its Roman office intact: the bird-reader whose verbs still forecast our futures.
normalIntro.cn: augur 完整保留了罗马官职：那位读鸟占卜的官员，其动词至今仍在为我们的未来占卦。

normal.en: augur well / augur ill: the two fixed phrases cover most modern uses.
normal.cn: augur well / augur ill 两个固定搭配涵盖了现代用法的大半。

normal.en: inaugurate is augur's brightest child: to found with the omens' blessing.
normal.cn: inaugurate 是 augur 最耀眼的孩子：在征兆祝福下开创。

normal.en: augury is the practice; the augur is the practitioner.
Spelling watch: auger drills holes, augur reads birds.
normal.cn: 拼写警戒：auger 钻孔，augur 观鸟。

normal.en: augment may share the increase root: growth and good omens once belonged together.
normal.cn: augment 或与 augur 同根：增长与吉兆古时同属一家。

abstract.en: Picture a man in a white cloak watching birds cross a square of sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一位白袍人注视飞鸟掠过一方天空。

abstract.en: The word is a raised hand halting an army until the sky approves.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一只抬起的手：天意未准，大军不发。

abstract.en: Every forecast is a tame descendant of augur.
abstract.cn: 每一次预测都是 augur 驯化后的后代。

examples.en: Empty shelves and long queues augur a hard winter.
examples.cn: 空荡的货架与排起的长队预示着艰难的冬天。

examples.en: The treaty's early troubles augured ill for the alliance.
examples.cn: 条约初期的种种波折对同盟而言是凶兆。

examples.en: In Rome the augurs read the sky before every election.
examples.cn: 在罗马，每次选举前占卜官都要观测天象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥格」——叫奥格的老祭司，每天格外观鸟占卜未来

root: 直接借自拉丁语 augur「占卜官」（相关词 augurium「征兆」、inaugurare「以兆祝圣」）；更早词根有争议：或为 avis「鸟」+ gar-/agere，或为意为「增长」的老词根（与 augere、augustus 相关），两说并存、不可强行选定，故须谨慎表述。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one word from the Roman sky to the modern headline: the official, his art, his verdicts, and the signs that survived the religion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随一个词从罗马天空走到现代新闻标题：那官职、那术数、那裁决，以及宗教消亡后仍存留的征兆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: birds crossing a marked square of sky, read as the future.
core.cn: 核心意象：飞鸟掠过划定的一方天区，被读出未来。

branches.en: THE OFFICE SIDE: the Roman augur and every later claimant of foresight.
branches.cn: 官职一面：罗马占卜官与后世一切先知式人物。

branches.en: THE ART SIDE: predicting and the whole practice of augury.
branches.cn: 术数一面：预断行为与占卜体系。

branches.en: THE MODERN SIDE: events that augur well or ill.
branches.cn: 现代一面：兆吉兆凶的事件本身。

branches.en: THE POWER SIDE: verdicts that stopped wars and elections.
branches.cn: 权力一面：能叫停战争与选举的裁决。

branches.en: THE RITE SIDE: inauguration as the augur's festive heir.
branches.cn: 仪式一面：作为占卜官节庆继承者的就职典礼。

intro.en: augur is a bare Latin borrowing with no prefix or suffix; its family lives in augury, augural, and inaugurate.
intro.cn: augur 是不带前后缀的拉丁语直接借词；其词族存于 augury、augural 与 inaugurate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin divination family centers on augur: augurium, augurare, and inaugurare all branch from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁占卜词族以 augur 为中心：augurium、augurare、inaugurare 皆由此分出。
